title: Alpha-compact objects retract from a bounded triangulated generator hull
statement: Let $C$ be a locally $v$-small triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with $v$-small coproducts and $\alpha$ a regular cardinal in universe $v$. Write $S$ for its maximal class of alpha-compact objects [def-sfb-alpha-compact-object]. Let $G,H$ be properties of objects such that $G\subseteq H\subseteq S$. Assume $H$ is replete, contains zero, is closed under integer shifts, distinguished-triangle extensions and coproducts with fewer than $\alpha$ summands. Assume every replete triangulated class containing $G$ and closed under all $v$-small coproducts contains every object of $C$. Then every object of $S$ is a retract of an object of $H$.

source.place: Krause (2001), Lemma 5(2) and the final paragraph, page 125: the localizing factor-through subcategory.

external.place: On Neeman’s Well Generated Triangulated Categories, Documenta Mathematica 6 (2001), pages 124–125.

proof.text: The maximal alpha-compact class S is replete, contains zero, and is shift closed by the API; its extension closure is supplied by the extension lemma. Let R(Y) mean that every map from an S-object into Y factors through an H-object. It contains H, is replete, contains zero, and is shift closed by the shift adjunction and the shift closure of S and H.

For a triangle Y0 to Y1 to Y2 with R(Y0) and R(Y1), factor the connecting composite X to Y2 to Y0[1] through H0 in H. A fiber X prime of X to H0 lies in S by extension closure. Complete to a morphism of triangles and factor the induced map X prime to Y1 through H1 in H. Form H2 as the cone of H0[-1] to H1. Two applications of triangle completion give X to H2 to Y2 agreeing with the given map on X prime. Their difference factors through H0 by exactness. Thus the original map factors through H2 plus H0, an H-object. This proves cone closure of R.

For a map from X in S to a coproduct of R-objects, G4 supplies S-component objects. Factor each component through H, then use alpha-smallness of X to restrict the map to fewer than alpha H-summands. Their coproduct belongs to H, proving coproduct closure of R.

R is therefore a replete localizing triangulated class containing G. The assumed generation property makes R all of C. Factor the identity of each X in S through H; the two maps exhibit X as a retract of an H-object.

proof_origin.place: Krause (2001), Lemma 5(2) and the final paragraph, page 125: the localizing factor-through subcategory.
